progression.authority: Server-recorded practical evidence; never lesson views, XP, streaks, payment, elapsed time or self-selected level.

progression.soft: Show Review First and, when delivery is enabled, Continue Anyway. A recommendation does not create an artificial lock.

distinctions.verified: The defined integrity and review process actually completed.

progression.primaryAndExploration: A primary path guides recommendations; exploratory work retains its own evidence and does not abandon the primary path.
progression.infrastructureFailure: Record an infrastructure result separately; do not penalize the learner or infer a skill gap from unavailable tests.
progression.unitRule: Required practice artifact, debugging explanation and transfer task meet their visible criteria; opening a lesson alone does not complete it.
progression.moduleRule: Required units, mandatory mission, visible behaviour requirements and practical assessment all satisfied; no blocking runtime defect.
progression.stageRule: All mandatory module, mission, project and checkpoint evidence required by the stage; optional work does not block completion.

assessment.rule: Every required criterion must be met. Quality informs feedback; bonus work cannot compensate for or block mandatory criteria. No universal percentage pass rule.
assessment.hiddenTests: Protected implementation may test only published requirements and their communicated edge cases. Never require arbitrary variable names or one architecture unless that architecture is the objective.
assessment.explanation: Judge code behaviour, choices, trade-offs and consequences. Do not grade English polish or spelling as programming competence.
assessment.debugging: Require reproduction, relevant observations, a cause-related fix, verified behaviour and an appropriate explanation. Do not grade speed.
assessment.modification: Use the learner’s existing solution, a new stated requirement, regression checks and explanation; do not ask for a complete rewrite as a shortcut.
assessment.retakes: Practice is freely repeatable. Low-stakes checkpoints allow retry after feedback. Verified retakes use an equivalent new scenario and the published assessment policy; no automatic irreversible failure.
assessment.history: Keep previous attempt, outcome, remediation and new attempt privately. Public evidence must not shame practice mistakes.
assessment.reviewerPrivacy: Keep reviewer notes, integrity telemetry and protected tests separate from this public curriculum. Do not include real protected assessment implementation in frontend artifacts.
assessment.codeCoach: Practice hints may identify a concept, diagnostic observation or next small step. During assessed work enforce allowed hint level; do not give complete solutions or hidden tests. Provider failures must not count as learner failure.

evidence.privacy: Private by default; publish only eligible evidence through explicit learner controls. Imported source is unverified and does not establish authorship.
evidence.recency: Retain Last Demonstrated and Last Verified with curriculum/technology context. Aging evidence prompts review, not arbitrary deletion or universal expiry.
evidence.diversity: Repeated evidence for one narrow competency cannot substitute for coverage of the level’s competency map.

promotion.Foundation: Purpose and fundamentals, guided practice, independent small solution and simple debugging from more than one activity.
promotion.Intermediate: Foundation evidence, multiple interacting-concept missions, a complete project, testing evidence and a practical checkpoint.
promotion.Advanced: Intermediate evidence plus unfamiliar feature, API, debugging, refactoring, testing, accessibility and architecture problems with justified trade-offs.
promotion.Professional: Substantial projects, production-style briefs, requirement changes, architecture, testing, accessibility, documentation and explanation. Public verified claims require corresponding verified evidence.
promotion.Specialist: Professional prerequisite, at least two distinct substantial verified projects, specialist investigation, unfamiliar codebase, domain-specific analysis, explanation, modification and verified practical review. Human assessment of depth is mandatory.

units.why: A browser needs a way to ask another computer for a document.
